svg.text: Extensions the interviewer may throw at you (multi-device + presence)
both are "free" because the base design already has CLIENT tables + pub/sub — that's the tell of a good base
Multi-device: "a person isn't offline — a device is"
· add the Client entity — (userId, clientId)
· inbox rows keyed by recipient CLIENT id
· pub/sub topics per client, not per user
· fan-out: for each participant × each device
(message delivered per-device, acked per-device)
the blow-up + the fix
100 people × 5 devices = 500 inbox rows > 100-row transaction
→ cap devices at 2–3 AND shrink group-size accordingly
percolate the cap through every surface: inbox, topics, groups
Presence — the little green orbs
· availability table: userId · status
connect → available · disconnect → unavailable
· cheap version: poll that table for my contacts
· live version: watchers SUBSCRIBE via pub/sub;
a status change publishes to the watchers' topics
the hard part is fan-out again
one user disconnecting must NOT notify 10 000 watchers
→ product decides who watches whom, and caps it
same constraint muscle as group size and device caps
Why these feel easy — and what that tells the interviewer
· multi-device is literally "change every key from user to client" — the Client entity was ALREADY in the design (v4 offline).
· presence just reuses the pub/sub machinery built for routing (deep dive 1b) plus a status table.
· extensions that slot in with ~no new components = a base design that chose the RIGHT abstractions.
name that sentence out loud — it's the senior/staff calibration the interviewer is listening for.
